payload.recallText: The third grade teacher wanted to be able to teach kids about the Oregon Trail but needed to make it interesting. She made stories to tell the kids daily for regular classes, but needed to make this lesson more interactive. She first took them on a walk through Manhattan for a couple of miles, even though the kids were hesitant and said they would just ride in the wagon, and one kid got thirsty along the way. She wanted to keep it authentic but didn't want to get in trouble with parents for not letting the kids have water, so she said "oh a stream, how unexpected" so that the kids would stay in the moment. The kids had a good time with it and every day they would be excited to go to class to learn more about the trail and their adventures. Every day before class, they would ask "is someone going to die today?" and she said that people died all the time on the trail, but they had been fortunate up until now. Then they arrived at the Rockies, and she wanted to keep the kids engaged, so she said that one of the students, Katie, got her legs stuck under the carriage and the legs got infected. She would have the kids roll a dice to decide their fates every day, and when Katie rolled the dice, it wasn't good and her leg infection got worse.
